skills.name: The Cold War: causes and manifestations

note.text: The Cold War appeared in policy, alliances, propaganda, economic competition, arms races and conflicts involving other countries. The Truman Doctrine in 1947 expressed American support against communist pressure; the Marshall Plan operated from 1948 to aid European recovery and support Western stability. Soviet leaders opposed American influence and consolidated their own bloc. NATO formed in 1949; the Warsaw Pact followed in 1955. The Berlin blockade and airlift of 1948–1949 showed confrontation over access without a direct general war between the superpowers.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to connect containment, aid, alliances, arms competition and proxy conflicts to the rivalry without treating every local war as wholly foreign-made. Builds on: the breakdown of the wartime alliance. Leads to: détente and attempts to manage superpower competition.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: The Cold War appeared in policy, alliances, propaganda, economic competition, arms races and conflicts involving other countries. The Truman Doctrine in {1947} expressed American support against communist pressure; the Marshall Plan operated from {1948} to aid European recovery and support Western stability. Soviet leaders opposed American influence and consolidated their own bloc. NATO formed in {1949}; the Warsaw Pact followed in {1955}. The Berlin blockade and airlift of {1948}–{1949} showed confrontation over access without a direct general war between the superpowers.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: Nuclear competition increased risks and encouraged deterrence: a state sought to prevent attack by threatening unacceptable costs. This was a strategy, not proof that weapons made everyone safe. The Korean War of {1950}–{1953} illustrates a conflict with local roots and major outside intervention. Propaganda promoted each bloc’s claims. Economic assistance could serve both recovery and strategic aims; it must not be reduced to one motive without evidence. Not every African government or nationalist movement simply followed orders from a superpower.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: For each manifestation state what happened and how it expressed rivalry. Separate alliance from aid, propaganda from military action and local objectives from outside intervention. The word cold refers to the absence of a full-scale direct US-Soviet war, not an absence of fighting elsewhere. Compare a policy’s announced purpose with its recipients, conditions and consequences.

key_words.meaning: policy using support and resources to limit perceived communist expansion
formal security alliances grouping states around rival powers
the blockade and airlift illustrating tension over access to the Western sectors
a war combining local struggles and major external military involvement

cards.idea: Distinguish the historical features before explaining their relationship.
example: containment and aid: policy using support and resources to limit perceived communist expansion.
military blocs: formal security alliances grouping states around rival powers.
Berlin confrontation: the blockade and airlift illustrating tension over access to the Western sectors.
conflict with outside intervention: a war combining local struggles and major external military involvement.

cards.idea: Connect a specific action or event to the historical feature it illustrates.
example: The United States pairs assistance with the aim of resisting communist influence.
NATO formed in {1949}; the Warsaw Pact formed in {1955}.
During {1948}–{1949}, an airlift supplied West Berlin amid the Soviet blockade of surface access.
In Korea, local division interacted with US-led UN and Chinese intervention within the wider rivalry.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: All economic aid was unrelated to political strategy. Correction: Aid could address recovery while also serving strategic objectives.
The Warsaw Pact was founded before NATO. Correction: Check the sequence: NATO preceded the Warsaw Pact.
The airlift was a programme for supplying a distant African plantation. Correction: It responded to the Berlin access crisis in occupied Germany.
Calling a war a Cold War conflict proves local causes and decisions did not exist. Correction: Outside involvement and local origins can both be part of an explanation.
